item.title: Whisky 3.5.2
item.description:
Bug-fix release: fresh installs work in every locale, DirectX 11 games run on default settings, and lost bottles come back.

  • Engine install fixed for day-first-date locales: first-run setup failed with "Archive contains unsafe path" on systems whose language formats dates day-first (UK, French, and many others). The archive safety check no longer depends on the system language.
  • DirectX 11 games work on default settings: the "Recommended" graphics backend now picks a translation layer the installed engine actually provides (DXMT, or DXVK) instead of one it doesn't ship, which made DX11 games fail to launch on a fresh install.
  • Backend picker honesty: D3DMetal is greyed out when the engine doesn't include it, and bottles already set to D3DMetal show a clear warning instead of games failing silently.
  • Lost bottles are recovered: bottles on disk that aren't in your library — after a reset registry or a restored backup — are detected at startup and offered for one-click re-import. A damaged bottle list is also backed up and recovered instead of being wiped.
  • Safer engine extraction: archives are unpacked and audited in a staging area, so a rejected archive leaves your existing installation untouched.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.5.1
item.description:
Bug-fix release: installing bottle dependencies now works out of the box.

  • Dependency installs fixed: installing components like the Visual C++ runtime, .NET, DirectX, and fonts (and the Winetricks verb browser) failed on a clean install because the winetricks tool was never bundled. It — and its verb catalog — now ship inside the app, so dependency installation works with no extra setup.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.5.0
item.description:
Quality-of-life improvements: clearer bottle settings, an optional menu-bar item, smoother bottle loading, and less intrusive update prompts.

  • Inline configuration help: bottle configuration options now show a one-line description of what each does — across the Wine section (Windows version, build, enhanced sync, DPI, Retina) and the DXVK section (DXVK, async, HUD).
  • Optional menu-bar extra (off by default, in Settings → General): launch a bottle's pinned programs, reopen Whisky, or quit without the main window — and keep Whisky and its running Wine processes alive after the window is closed.
  • Scanning a bottle for installed programs now runs off the main thread, so opening or switching to a large bottle no longer hitches the UI.
  • Gentler update reminders: a scheduled background check that finds a new version shows a Dock badge and an "Install Update…" menu item instead of a focus-stealing dialog.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.4.0
item.description:
Per-bottle DXMT (Direct3D 11 → Metal) — an experimental graphics backend you can pick per bottle or per program — plus reliability fixes.

  • DXMT (Experimental): a new Direct3D 11 → Metal backend, selectable per bottle/program from the graphics picker and deployed like DXVK so it never affects other bottles. D3DMetal remains the recommended default; the backend card prompts you to update the runtime when it's needed.
  • Installing or updating the Wine runtime no longer erases the rest of Whisky's Application Support folder.
  • Per-program graphics overrides now reliably win over the bottle's setting.
  • A launch error for a program opened from Finder now surfaces as a notification instead of failing silently.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.3.0
item.description:
Crash-safe, forward-compatible bottle settings, hardened icon parsing, and optional opt-in anonymous telemetry.

  • Bottle and per-program settings are now written atomically, so a crash mid-save can no longer wipe your configuration.
  • Settings written by a newer Whisky load gracefully — an unrecognized choice falls back to its default instead of failing to load the whole bottle.
  • An unreadable settings file is now preserved (moved aside for recovery) instead of being silently overwritten.
  • Hardened icon and thumbnail extraction against crafted or corrupt Windows executables that could previously crash or hang the parser.
  • Optional, opt-in anonymous usage telemetry (off by default) to surface first-run install failures — no personal data, paths, or error text is ever sent.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.2.0
item.description:
Verified Wine downloads, plus clearer and earlier errors when something goes wrong.

  • The Wine runtime download is now verified against a published SHA-256 before install — a corrupted or truncated download is caught and retried instead of unpacking a broken runtime.
  • Bottle creation validates the chosen location up front: a non-writable folder or a nearly-full disk now gives a clear error instead of the bottle silently disappearing.
  • Runtime install failures surface their specific cause (missing tarball, disk full, extraction failure) instead of being swallowed.
  • A half-installed runtime is now detected and prompts a clean re-install instead of leaving every bottle to fail with cryptic Wine errors.
  • Bottle-creation error messages are now localizable.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.1.0
item.description:
One-click migration from the original Whisky, ~50 more supported games, and reliability fixes.

  • File → Migrate from the Original Whisky imports your existing bottles in place, non-destructively.
  • Fixes a bug where an idle Wine process could peg a CPU core.
  • ~50 new bundled GameDB entries with one-click recommended configs (now 79 titles).
  • Wine inherits the host timezone; display sleep is suppressed during play; host fonts are copied so Unity titles render text.

See the release notes for the full changelog.

item.title: Whisky 3.0.1
item.description:
Fixes a pipe deadlock in Tar.validateArchivePaths that caused the WhiskyWine installer to hang at "Installing WhiskyWine — Almost there." Tar's verbose listing for the 313 MB Libraries archive overflowed the OS pipe buffer; Whisky now drains the pipe before waiting for tar to exit.

See the release notes for the full changelog.
